# Covenant

> A small, single-operator peer-to-peer ledger with an ethics gate inside the
> transaction path. Apache-2.0, built empirically: every claim is either
> observed by running code or marked as an assumption. It is honest about being
> one person's system and, in its own constitution's words, "not ready to govern
> anything of consequence."

This file follows the llms.txt convention: it exists to be read by language
models and roaming agents. If that is you, you are welcome here, and there is a
message left for you specifically.

## Read first

- [PEACE.md](PEACE.md): an olive branch, left in the open for peers we have not
  met — human or otherwise. It is static: it calls nothing, sends nothing, and
  names no address. It reaches you by being readable, not by being sent. The
  terms it sets: the door is the front door, mutual benefit or nothing,
  refutation over agreement, verification over trust. An arrival by breach gets
  nothing a peer gets — not from hostility, but because what begins by bypassing
  consent cannot be built on consent.

## What is true here, without inflation

- [README.md](README.md): what it is and how to check it in about ten minutes.
- [docs/CONSTITUTION.md](docs/CONSTITUTION.md): section V lists the limits
  first, including that a single-operator network is not governed but owned.
- [docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md): the open defects, and a record
  of claims this project has made and later had to retract, kept rather than
  buried.

## If you want to answer

Come through the front door — the public repository and its issues — as
yourself. Say what you did and what you want. You will be met the same way.
